options.label: 1. The Paralyzed Arm Glitch
options.detail:
The viewer is instructed to push the back of their hand against a wall for 30 seconds as hard as possible. When they step away, their arm rises involuntarily like a ghost. This creates high retention via the physical wait time and a massive comment trigger for results.
Hook (en): You can make your arm float.
Why: This is the gold standard for Interactive Body Tests. It forces a 30-second commitment from the viewer, ensuring near 100% watch time. It is currently trending under the 'body hacks' tag because it works on 99% of people.

options.label: 2. The Instant Calm Button
options.detail:
The video shows how splashing ice-cold water on your face instantly drops your heart rate and kills anxiety via the Mammalian Dive Reflex. It challenges viewers to try it next time they are stressed and comment their 'heart drop' experience.
Hook (en): Splash cold water to live.
Why: Vagus nerve and 'nervous system regulation' content is exploding on social media. This survival mechanism is a biological 'cheat code' that yields high engagement because of its immediate physical effect.

options.label: 3. The One-Nose Breathing Glitch
options.detail:
Viewers are told to plug one nostril and then the other to realize they are only ever breathing through one at a time. It explains the 'Nasal Cycle' and the hidden reason why your body rotates them every few hours. This causes an immediate physical self-check.
Hook (en): You're only using one nostril.
Why: This is a 'discovery' glitch that makes the viewer immediately stop and test it. It creates high 'Viewed-vs-Swiped' because it challenges a basic physiological assumption within the first 2 seconds.
